name: Youth rights
summary: Youth rights holds that people are denied basic civil and human rights because of their young age, a prejudice it calls ageism or adultism. It demands the vote, free speech, bodily and medical autonomy, control over education, freedom from physical punishment and curfews, and an end to age restrictions generally. It is a campaign about age and does not set out a programme on the economy, the state or foreign affairs.
scope: The liberationist youth rights position as set out by the National Youth Rights Association (the main US organisation, its issue pages and Youth Rights 101) and described in scholarship on children's liberationism (SEP, citing Holt, Farson and Cohen). It excludes the protectionist children's rights tradition, which gives children welfare rights but not full freedom rights, and anything the sources do not tie to the age-based rights campaign.

notes: Evidence is almost wholly from NYRA's issue pages (school, voting, medical, labor, driving, drinking age, censorship, juvenile justice, parenting, social media), which speak to age-based rights and say nothing on economy, government structure, world affairs, ecology or technology. Themes searched: economy (labor page criticises the youth sub-minimum wage but states no wage policy), liberty, society (sex education appears only as a harm of parental restriction), government, world. The SEP notes liberationists divide on whether the very young have rights, so only statements settled by NYRA's stated positions are answered.
